note: Yes. The wave contract at Setup and Mother Ship/assurance-2026-10-05/IMPLEMENTATION-PLAN.md:37 states the cached-read behaviour in mechanism terms (real server, cookie auth, Event-gated observe, bounded cached GETs, publish-after-release), and the same plan's required-id paragraphs plus H1-H6 are specific enough to judge the supplied code and tests. Reviewer family: grok. H5 is a measurement, not a defect: a cold snapshot(True) with four installed CLIs blocks the caller until 13 hidden commands finish (four --version, ChatGPT help/schema/probe/observe, Claude help/status/observe, and model_policy.discover at model_policy.py:204-244); test_repeated_cached_page_load records that count. The supplied wave diff changes only handle_get login routing (provider_setup.py:543) and adds the rigor file; no existing assertion is weakened. The five required ids hit the real server or the real adapter seams they name; the strict xfails below fail for the reason their markers state.

findings.message: H4 confirmed. private_account_path is true only when the resolved path is under data_dir/.anchor/provider-accounts. Default credential homes (Path.home()/.codex, .claude, .grok, and a CODEX_HOME or CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR redirect) fail that check. resolve_project_artifact then rejects only a top component of .git or .anchor (report_viewer.py:335) and, when private_account_path is false (report_viewer.py:401-403), returns the file bytes (report_viewer.py:417). GET /artifact/ is AUTH_OPEN (route_table.py:164). The auth pillar defaults to open (pillar_flags.py:11), so _data_plane_gate does not 401 a tokenless request (anchor_gui.py:22458-22470) and the legacy handler writes those bytes (anchor_gui.py:23220-23225). The same helper gap is on handle_ecgberht_artifact (anchor_gui.py:14622-14650), handle_project_file_content (anchor_gui.py:19831-19868), and steward deliverable-file (steward_cockpit/steward_routes.py:991-996). tests/test_provider_setup.py:825-845 plants its canary only under the isolated provider-accounts home, which this check already blocks. Registering the user home as the project and requesting the planted auth.json returns the credential body. test_h4 is an honest failing reproduction: its first route assertion sees that body.

H1 confirmed. apply() raises 'Selected account is unready for execution' whenever the selected account's execution.ready is false, before it looks at which preference field changed. ready requires auth == signed_in and a native observation younger than TTL (provider_setup.py:204-207). The selected account for a threshold-only save is still default_cli's account, because family stays null (provider_setup.py:258). Aging observations[key]['observed_at'] past TTL, a refresh that stored auth timeout, or a new ProviderService whose observation map is empty all make ready false, so warning_threshold is never written. test_h1_threshold_only_save_does_not_need_a_fresh_ready_account is an honest strict-xfail: the cold branch fails at this raise with quality still empty, so the catalog check is not involved.

H2 confirmed. apply() walks every saved prefs['quality'] entry and raises 'Refresh native model capabilities before choosing an exact model or effort' when that entry is an exact model or effort and the catalog state is not fresh. snapshot() forces catalog state to stale once observed_at is older than TTL (provider_setup.py:209-210). A save that only changes warning_threshold still hits this loop. The stack fixture's discover result includes balanced/high (tests/test_provider_setup.py:85-87), so the first apply in test_h2_threshold_only_save_does_not_revalidate_unchanged_quality succeeds and the assertion at rigor line 702 sees the stale catalog; the second apply is the failing reproduction.

W1-E1 confirmed. start_login calls refresh and then starts a native login unless the observation that refresh just stored has auth == signed_in (provider_setup.py:287-289). On NativeError, refresh overwrites auth with the error state (provider_setup.py:160) while leaving the credential files in the home. A timeout, expiry, or unavailable status read therefore removes the signed-in guard the comment at provider_setup.py:285-286 requires, and NativeProviders.login runs a credential-replacing command in that home (provider_native.py:389-438). The Setup button enables Sign in whenever auth is not signed_in (static/provider-setup.js:43). test_w1e1_failed_status_read_does_not_disarm_the_signed_in_guard is an honest strict-xfail: after a signed-in refresh, setting backend.failed and backend.timeout makes start_login return an attempt and sets login_started.

H3 confirmed. A successful observe that returns allowance state unknown or unsupported, with no windows and no tokens, still takes the else branch and stamps observed_at (provider_setup.py:153-154). The failure path then sets state to stale for every metric that has observed_at (provider_setup.py:163). The page prints 'Stale report retained' for any stale allowance (static/provider-setup.js:22). test_h3_never_supported_report_is_not_relabelled_stale is an honest strict-xfail on chatgpt-default: the second refresh's allowance state is stale. Claude is a second shape of the same bug: provider_setup.py:155-156 replaces allowance with claude_allowance, which leaves observed_at null when there is no signal, so the failure path relabels that permanent unsupported allowance to the error state (timeout, expired, unavailable, or error).

H6 confirmed. When native login returns and the follow-up refresh stores an auth other than signed_in, the worker raises NativeError (provider_setup.py:312-314) and the except block reports state failed with 'Native sign-in failed or timed out' (provider_setup.py:316-318). The credentials are already in the home, so the next start_login hits the signed-in guard (provider_setup.py:288-289). test_h6_completed_login_with_failed_status_read_is_reported_honestly is an honest strict-xfail: the pytest.raises for 'already signed in' passes, then the assertion that status state is completed fails.

The Cave and High Seat capacity rail still builds its single Claude row from latest_limit_signal() called with no connection id (usage_capacity.py:278). The row note states that two accounts cannot be told apart (usage_capacity.py:256). anchor_gui._capacity_rows (anchor_gui.py:8137-8142) puts that rail into the seat context. separate-account-allowance-attribution proves ProviderService.snapshot and latest_limit_signal(connection_id=...) only. The browser half of failure-keeps-existing-session-and-quality replaces the seat context capacity with an empty list (tests/test_provider_setup_rigor.py:622), so that pass never renders this rail.

repro.command: python -c "import usage_capacity; import inspect; src=inspect.getsource(usage_capacity.anchor_seen); assert 'latest_limit_signal(now, j)' in src"

findings.message: capability(family, refresh=True) returns the cached probe for the whole TTL, including a probe stored as state error and isolated false (provider_setup.py:93 and provider_setup.py:101-106). Both refresh() (provider_setup.py:127) and add() (provider_setup.py:235) call capability with refresh=True. A transient capability failure therefore refuses a new isolated account for 300 seconds and an explicit refresh does not run a new native probe. None of the five required ids retries add() inside that window.

repro.command: python -c "import provider_setup; import inspect; src=inspect.getsource(provider_setup.ProviderService.capability); assert 'not refresh or time.time() - existing' in src"

findings.message: unsupported-is-not-usable's browser check requires both 'Not reported' and the allowance state word inside #provider-detail. Those substrings are present on every account row: 'Exact tokens remaining' is the constant 'Not reported' (static/provider-setup.js:14), api_spend.state is always unsupported (provider_setup.py:225, rendered at static/provider-setup.js:18), and a missing CLI renders the words 'CLI unavailable' (static/provider-setup.js:34). The assertion that does bind to this row is the absence of a '% remaining' phrase, which is how real windows are drawn (static/provider-setup.js:20). The positive phrase check does not establish that this row's allowance.state is the text on screen. The server-side capacity, execution.ready, selected_for_launch, and require_capacity_choice checks in the same test do establish their contract clauses.
